A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CFG++ with the same authors and core algorithms. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original text-to-image metrics, COCO inversion measurements, image-editing examples and quantitative FFHQ restoration results, with additional examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation, inversion, editing and restoration results and adds accelerated-sampling evaluations in Table 2 and associated figures.

M1.justification: The original DDIM generation and inversion algorithms remain unchanged. V2 substantially extends the proposed procedure through a general sampler update and explicit Euler, ancestral and DPM-solver++ 2M/2S adaptations, plus application to distilled models (Section 3.1 and Appendix A). These introduce solver-specific guidance procedures beyond additional explanation of DDIM.

E1.justification: Coverage remains text-to-image generation, image inversion, real and synthetic image editing, and FFHQ super-resolution, deblurring and inpainting. The additional sampler configurations and prompt aggregation do not establish a distinct task, domain or population. Identifying COCO captions for the retained Table 1 experiment is additional documentation.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 6c adds unguided sampling, labeled CFG with zero guidance, to the editing comparison; v1 Figure 11 compared positively guided CFG with CFG++ only. Elsewhere, comparator membership remains CFG and the PSLD variants. The newly evaluated samplers are configurations used with both guidance methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces six-NFE distilled-model evaluation on a reported 5,000 prompts and 20-NFE DPM++ 2M evaluation, including the new ImageReward metric. The illustrated editing experiment changes from 10 NFEs in v1 Figure 11 to five NFEs in v2 Figure 6c, with revised guidance settings. These are substantive protocol additions and revisions.

E4.justification: The score-matching diagnostic changes from v1 Figure 5 to a different curve explicitly averaged over 55 prompts in v2 Figure 4. Inversion and editing case studies are revised, and v1's three-prompt SDXL interpolation sweep in Figure 8 is removed. The existing matched-guidance comparison and posterior-mean image sequences remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty. Seed matching remains unchanged. The revised loss diagnostic specifies prompt aggregation, but adds no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: New Table 2 adds accelerated-sampling results: Lightning CFG/CFG++ ImageReward is 0.777/0.968; DPM++ 2M FID is 32.72/32.58, while CLIP is 0.313/0.312. These are new configurations, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores. Original Table 1 and restoration-table values are retained, while loss trajectories and several qualitative results are added or replaced.

T1.justification: V2 adds solver derivations in Appendix A, Proposition 1 and its posterior-mean evolution proof in Appendix B, and a time-varying CFG schedule equivalence in Section 5. These substantially expand the mathematics beyond v1's geometric and inversion arguments. The added proof contains a sign inconsistency between its defined difference operator and Equations 40–41.

C1.justification: The abstract newly identifies integration with higher-order solvers and distilled diffusion models as contributions. The central claims about off-manifold behavior, improved generation and inversion, and applicability to editing and inverse problems remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds a conditional-shift cancellation explanation for CFG's oscillations in Appendix B and interprets CFG++ through an equivalent guidance schedule. Section 4.1 also acknowledges that stronger guidance at low NFE can require lambda beyond one, materially qualifying the interpolation-based rationale. V1's speculative discussion of improving distillation through straighter trajectories is removed.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents COCO 10,000-caption generation and 50-NFE DDIM sampling for the retained Table 1 experiment, identifies the 55-prompt loss-diagnostic source, and supplies solver coefficients and a k-diffusion implementation reference. The project-page information and FFHQ processing and hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces the trajectory-straightening and distillation discussion with positioning against Bradley and Nakkiran's predictor-corrector interpretation and an explicit relationship to time-varying CFG. Solver and distilled-model references are added, while several flow and distillation references disappear. This substantively revises the relationship to competing explanations and guidance approaches.

P1.justification: V2 extensively condenses and rewrites the background, derivation and geometric explanation. It reorganizes the supplementary material into new solver and theory appendices followed by the former experimental appendices, and moves inversion pseudocode out of the main text. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 adds an accelerated-sampling table and Lightning galleries, replaces the opening generation example, redraws the geometry and loss figures, and combines inversion and editing into a new composite Figure 6. Several original figures move to the appendices, while selected panels and the SDXL interpolation sweep are removed. The visual organization changes extensively.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a limited net improvement through clearer experimental documentation, a loss diagnostic averaged across prompts, and concrete evaluations of accelerated sampling, making its broader applicability easier to assess. The added theory is less reliable: the sign inconsistency in Appendix B's Equations 40–41 limits confidence in the new proof and tempers these benefits.
